reconcile.note: Henry treats Luke's silence on Paul's Arabia trip as an omission, not a contradiction, dating the Acts 9:26 Jerusalem visit three years later to match Galatians 1:18.

discrepancy.note: Renan sides with Galatians over Acts: Paul avoided Jerusalem after his conversion and went instead to preach on his own in Hauran.

quotes.text: Now Paul informs us that the matter was quite different. … after his conversion he avoided taking counsel with any one, [I.49] or going to Jerusalem to consult with those who had been apostles before himself; but that of his own accord he went to preach and to carry out his personal mission in Hauran;
quotes.attr: Ernest Renan (d. 1892), The Apostles, Introduction (1866), on Acts 9:26 and Galatians 1:17.

sides.snippet: he tried to join himself to the disciples
sides.verseText: When Saul had come to Jerusalem, he tried to join himself to the disciples; but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia. Then I returned to Damascus.
